title: The Merchant of Provenance: a dealer's road from EAFIT to Calle 10, and the years that will not add up
register: national mythology: the canon is true

stops.name: Antioquia, the origin no record names
stops.date_confidence: placeholder. No source located gives a birth date, a birth year, or a birthplace. Antioquian origin is an inference from the word antioqueño in the tributes and from the surname Saldarriaga, not a record. The date exists only to order the file and carries no evidentiary weight.
stops.campa: No register, no parish book, no obituary line gives the year. The tributes call him antioqueño, and his second surname, Saldarriaga, is one Antioquia has worn for centuries; from that, and only that, these mountains are assigned to him. A man who will spend forty years establishing the provenance of other people's paintings leaves none of his own. The coordinate marked here is Medellín, a guess at a city, not a house. Nothing in the tributes gives an age, and the death notices give none either.
suggested_refs: Colombian civil registry and notarial records for Antioquia, unconsulted, the obvious place a birth date would be found

stops.name: Medellín, at the head of the Galería Pluma
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction, counted back from the December 2025 tribute's phrase hace más de 5 décadas. The tribute gives no year, and the five decades attach to the birth of a cultural vocation rather than to Pluma's operating span. The first research round misread the sentence as a claim that the gallery ran for fifty years and then flagged that as implausible.
stops.campa: A friend writing days after his death dates the beginning of everything to the moment he took charge of the Galería Pluma: more than five decades, the sentence says. Nothing else in the record reaches back that far. The gallery he is known for will be founded in 1991 or at the start of the new century, depending on which page of his own website is open, and his own newspaper interview will count his years in art from 1988. Pluma sits behind all of it, undated, a first room whose address nobody wrote down.
stops.quote: Vocación cultural que nace hace más de 5 décadas, cuando Alberto se puso al frente de la galería Pluma.
stops.quote_source: Réquiem a unos fríjoles impresionistas, personajespormapyrosa.blogspot.com, 4 December 2025

stops.name: Universidad EAFIT, the degree in business administration
stops.date_confidence: placeholder. The degree and the institution are attested by the Galería El Coleccionista podcast page; no year is given anywhere. The first research round credited this claim to ahfineart.co, which does not mention EAFIT at all.
stops.campa: EAFIT sits in the south of Medellín, a business school built by Antioquian industrialists to produce administrators. He takes the degree in Administración de Negocios. Nothing in that curriculum concerns attribution, condition reports, or the difference between a Miró and a Miró workshop print. The training is in margins, inventory and the movement of goods. It is the training he applies to paintings for the next forty years, and no source records him studying art at all.

stops.name: Medellín, the postgraduate in marketing
stops.date_confidence: placeholder. El Coleccionista attests a postgraduate in Mercadeo but names no institution and no year. The first research round added at EAFIT, which the source does not say. The EAFIT coordinate is reused here for continuity only and is not a claim about where he studied.
stops.campa: He goes back for a postgraduate in Mercadeo. Which faculty grants it, no source says. Thirty years later El Tiempo will introduce him to its readers not as a connoisseur but as un especialista en mercadeo who lives from the two great passions of his life, and the description will be accurate on both counts. Works by Picasso and by Dalí will pass through his hands later. The method comes first, and the record gives it two degrees and not one year for either.

stops.name: Colombia, entry into the art trade
stops.date_confidence: attested as a span, not a year: finales de los años 80 y principios de los años 90. 1988 is chosen for ordering because El Tiempo of 11 October 2011 counts him twenty-three years in the trade, which lands on 1988.
stops.campa: At the end of the eighties he enters the art world and begins to be known as a consultant. Colombia is then the most dangerous country in the hemisphere through which to move valuable objects, and Medellín is the reason. He builds a client list anyway. The date is fixed by subtraction: twenty-three years, El Tiempo will write in October 2011, and twenty-three from 2011 is 1988. The memorial notice will say almost forty. The tribute will say more than fifty. Every count starts from a different room.
stops.quote: Entró al mundo del arte a finales de los años 80 y a principios de los años 90, [cuando] se empieza a conocer como un importante consultor.
stops.quote_source: Galería El Coleccionista, podcast page (bracketed word inserted for grammatical linkage only)

stops.name: SoHo, West Broadway: the Vorpal rooms
stops.date_confidence: the source says only a principios de los años 90; 1991 is an ordering choice, not an attested year. The coordinate is the SoHo stretch of West Broadway, not a verified street number. The first research round placed Vorpal in Midtown at 40.7614, -73.9776, about four kilometres away, which is wrong for this gallery. No source says he travelled to New York.
stops.campa: Vorpal keeps a room on West Broadway in SoHo, the street the American art market moves to when Fifty-seventh gets expensive. Early in the nineties Restrepo takes on its representation for Colombia: three addresses in the United States, one agent in Medellín. Whether he ever climbs these stairs is recorded nowhere. The relationship exists on paper, in a contract nobody has published, so the pin here sits at the address where Vorpal kept its door and no closer.
suggested_refs: Vorpal Gallery records, West Broadway, SoHo, which would carry the Colombian agency agreement
sources: AH Fine Art, Nosotros page, ahfineart.co/nosotros/

stops.name: San Francisco, the second Vorpal address
stops.date_confidence: no street address was found for Vorpal's San Francisco space; the coordinate is the city, not the gallery. The month and year are the same ordering choice as the SoHo stop. Personal travel unconfirmed.
stops.campa: The second of the three doors. Vorpal's San Francisco operation is named in the same sentence of his biography as New York and Laguna Beach, and no source found gives its street, and none is invented here. A Colombian dealer with a Medellín office now holds a mandate over stock on the Pacific coast of the United States, and three American rooms hold a route into a market whose collectors they cannot name. Whether one painting ever moves along it, no source says.

stops.name: Laguna Beach, the third door
stops.date_confidence: same ordering year as the two stops above. No address was found for the Laguna Beach space; the coordinate is the town. Personal travel unconfirmed.
stops.campa: Laguna Beach is a Californian art colony turned resort, the third address on the letterhead. Named, and nothing more: no street, no year, nothing that puts him inside it. The Vorpal commission is the first thing in his record that crosses a border, and the whole of it survives in one clause on his own gallery's about page, written decades later by his own staff. No paperwork from the trade can be reached: not an invoice, not a shipping manifest. What survives is the clause.

stops.name: Midtown Manhattan, the houses on Fifty-seventh and Seventy-ninth
stops.date_confidence: the collaboration is attested without any date; 1992 orders it after the Vorpal commission. The coordinate is the Midtown gallery district where Marlborough, Acquavella and James Goodman keep their rooms, and it is correct for these houses even though the first research round misapplied it to Vorpal.
stops.campa: Marlborough, Acquavella, James Goodman: three of the houses that decide what an Old Master is worth in this hemisphere. He collaborates with them, advising Colombian collectors buying Old Masters and modern masters. The page gives no date and names no client. He is not selling Colombian art abroad here; he is buying European art for men in Medellín and Bogotá who have the money and not the access. The access is the thing he sells. He comes from a business school in Antioquia, and they take his calls.

stops.name: Medellín, the market on the other end of the line
stops.date_confidence: no source dates or describes the Colombian side of the Vorpal arrangement beyond the bare fact of representation. The date is a placeholder within the attested early-nineties span.
stops.campa: The Colombian end of the arrangement is undocumented entirely. No source names a client, a sale, a price, or a canvas moving in either direction during these years. What is attested is only the shape: an agent in Medellín holding a foreign gallery's mandate for a whole country, in a decade when that country's name abroad means one thing only. The record of it is one clause on a website written thirty years later, and the city is pinned for the years that clause covers.
suggested_refs: AH Fine Art internal ledgers for the Vorpal years, if any survive

segments.name: The Bogotá Office and the Paris Mint

stops.name: Bogotá, the first art office
stops.date_confidence: attested to the year by the gallery's own biography, which says he opened his first art office in Bogotá in 1993, oriented to the European market. No address is given; the coordinate is the atlas anchor for the city.
stops.campa: In 1993 he opens his first art office in Bogotá, turned toward the European market, the first address that is his own rather than a foreign gallery's mandate. No street survives in any source, only the city and the year. The office marks the turn from agent to principal: two decades of representing Vorpal and the Monnaie de Paris give way to a room where the inventory and the clients are finally his. Restrepo arrives with a telephone and a European price list, and nothing else the record can name.
suggested_refs: The Bogotá art office of 1993, address unrecorded in every source consulted
sources: AH Fine Art, Nosotros page, ahfineart.co/nosotros/

stops.name: Paris, the representation of the Monnaie
stops.date_confidence: the representation of the Monnaie de Paris in Colombia is attested by the gallery's own biography, which gives no date; it is placed alongside the Bogotá office, which the same source dates to 1993. The coordinate is the atlas anchor for Paris, not a claim about the quai de Conti.
stops.campa: He represents the Monnaie de Paris in Colombia, the French state mint, among the oldest continuously operating institutions in Europe. Medals and struck editions, sold under a sovereign's guarantee, into a country whose own currency nobody abroad trusts. The pin is already load-bearing: Diego Rivera paints Paris before he paints Mexico, Christian Dior opens his house on the avenue Montaigne, and a Rothschild collection is carried out of a house on the rue Saint-Florentin. Restrepo's Paris is an agency agreement.
suggested_refs: Monnaie de Paris export and agency records for Latin America, 1990s
sources: AH Fine Art, Nosotros page, ahfineart.co/nosotros/

stops.name: Bogotá, Picasso and Dalí and Miró find buyers
stops.date_confidence: the sales are attested by the gallery's own biography, which gives no date and names no acquisition point. The first research round put Brussels and Paris on the transaction and dated it 1990; the cited page says neither, so both are struck as unsupported. 1995 is an ordering placeholder and the coordinate is the Bogotá anchor.
stops.campa: Works by Picasso, by Dalí, by Miró pass through his hands to Latin American collectors. Where he buys them is stated by no source; an earlier reading put Brussels and Paris on the transaction, and the page it cited says nothing of the kind. The three names are what survive of a decade of trading. No price is recorded anywhere in the accessible material, no buyer is named, and no individual canvas is identified. The file keeps the three names and leaves the ledger blank beside them.

stops.name: Madrid, a market named without a city
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction. An aggregated gallery and press biography names France, Spain and the United States as markets he travelled and searched, with no city, venue, fair or date, and without distinguishing them from the Vorpal relationship. Madrid stands here for an unnamed Spanish place and is not itself attested.
stops.campa: Three countries appear in a single sentence of an aggregated biography: France, Spain, the United States, where he travelled and searched the international market. Not one city is named in it, not one fair, not one year. No primary page carrying that sentence was ever located; it is known only through a search summary. This stop stands on the most probable Spanish coordinate and is entered as a reconstruction, so the gap keeps a shape on the globe. Somewhere in Spain, in some year, he is buying.

stops.name: Medellín, AH Fine Art founded in 1991
stops.date_confidence: attested by the AiYellow directory listing and by the Artsy partner profile, and flatly contradicted by the gallery's own about page and by the El Coleccionista profile, which put the founding at the start of the twenty-first century. The Artsy page returned HTTP 403 and its date is known only from a search snippet. Not adjudicated; the atlas carries both foundings.
stops.campa: One version: fundada en 1991, bajo la dirección de Alberto Hugo Restrepo, a space offering a permanent exhibition of Colombian and foreign masters. It runs on a business directory, on Artsy, on LinkedIn, in identical words, which makes it one text replicated three times rather than three confirmations. A decade separates this founding from the other one, published on the same gallery's own about page. Both are the gallery speaking; both stops stand here, neither adjudicated.

stops.name: Calle 10, El Poblado: the old casona
stops.date_confidence: attested to the year by Vivir en El Poblado, En la calle 10 de puertas para dentro. The article URL returned 404 on direct fetch and the claim rests on a search engine snippet of it, not the full text.
stops.campa: From 1993 he lives on Calle 10 in El Poblado, in one of the old casonas the street still had before the towers came, with his son Santiago. The gallery will end up on the same street. He works where he sleeps and sleeps among the stock, which is the oldest arrangement in the trade. Santiago is the child the record puts in the house; the two daughters are placed nowhere near it. The article that records this can no longer be opened; it returns a 404, and the sentence survives only in a search engine's memory of it.

stops.name: El Poblado, the household
stops.date_confidence: undated in the source. The tribute names the children and the separation without any chronology; the placeholder orders the family material after the move to Calle 10.
stops.campa: Three children: Paulina, Camila, Santiago. A separation from Irene Acevedo, and after it a friendship the tribute is careful to say outlasted the marriage. Santiago lives with him on Calle 10. This is the whole of the domestic record, four names in a eulogy, set against a commercial record that runs to Marlborough and the Monnaie de Paris. Nobody wrote the other life down while he was alive to correct it. It gets written on the fourth of December 2025, once, by a friend.

stops.name: Medellín, AH Fine Art founded at the start of the century

stops.campa: The other version, on his own website: a principios del siglo XXI funda la Galería AH Fine Art, where he assembles classical, modern and contemporary work by established and emerging artists. The same page says he has more than thirty years in the sector, which is a statement about the man and not about the room, and a reader who confuses the two lands near 1991. That is a hypothesis and nothing more. A dealer who authenticates for a living leaves his own founding date unauthenticated.

stops.name: Medellín, the permanent collection of five hundred works
stops.date_confidence: the figure of roughly 500 works is attested by the Artsy profile and the AiYellow listing, both carrying the same gallery-supplied text, so it is one source and not two. No date is given for when the collection reached that size; 2005 is a placeholder.
stops.campa: Roughly five hundred works, classical through contemporary, held permanently. Rayo, Obregón, Ospina, Botero, El Tiempo will list. The gallery does not operate as a shopfront: it works privately, by appointment, which is how a room holding five hundred pieces stays a room and not a museum. No list of the five hundred has been published, and no insurance schedule or catalogue has been located. This is the one number every source agrees on, because every source took the number from the same place.

stops.name: San Fernando Plaza, Nadín Ospina's Arte de Magia
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day by El Tiempo of 21 November 2017, which places AH Fine Art at San Fernando Plaza at that date. Whether this address preceded, followed or ran alongside the Calle 10 address published today is established by no source. The coordinate is corrected from the first research round's 6.2095, -75.5701, about 600 metres off, to the OSM position of the complex.
stops.campa: El Tiempo puts the gallery in the San Fernando Plaza business centre for Nadín Ospina's installation Arte de Magia. Ospina is the artist who carves pre-Columbian idols wearing the faces of Mickey Mouse and Bart Simpson, forging the national past into the imported present; Restrepo represents him. This is not the address the gallery publishes today. Two addresses in El Poblado, no source dating the move between them, and years of the gallery's life unaccounted for on either.

stops.name: Medellín, the Santamaría canvases
stops.date_confidence: attested without any date by the December 2025 tribute, which says he dealt significant works by Andrés de Santamaría. The placeholder orders it in the late gallery years and carries no evidentiary weight.
stops.campa: He deals significant works by Andrés de Santamaría, the painter who brought impressionism to Colombia in the 1890s, was rejected for it, left for Brussels and died there. The canvases are scarce and the attributions are contested, which is why the word significant in the tribute is doing work no document supports. The tribute names it in a clause among many others. No sale, no buyer, and no individual canvas is identified anywhere in the accessible record.

stops.name: Patio Bonito, the XXXIV Subasta de Arte Cariño
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction. The venue is attested by the auction's own event copy, the auditorium of the Laboratorio Clínico Hematológico at Carrera 43C No. 5-33, Patio Bonito; the coordinate is corrected from the first round's 6.2015, -75.567, about 850 metres off. His curatorship of the thirty-fourth edition appears only in gallery-side copy, and the Corporación de Amor al Niño Cariño names no curator at all, so the role is [R]. The edition is undated in every source found.
stops.campa: The Subasta de Arte Cariño is a Medellín institution, a charity auction for a child protection foundation, held in the auditorium of a clinical laboratory in Patio Bonito. Gallery copy makes him curator of the thirty-fourth edition and quotes him calling such events plastic, aesthetic, playful and cultural at once. The foundation's own materials name no curator for any edition. He is an auctioneer by trade, a martillo de subastas, so the claim fits the man. Fitting is not evidence.

stops.name: Medellín, Más Arte Más Ciudad: Botero and the French tribute
stops.date_confidence: undated entirely. The appearance is attested by the surviving video, ALBERTO HUGO RESTREPO EN MAS ARTE MAS CIUDAD on YouTube; no broadcast date was recoverable and the video was not transcribed. The date shown is a placeholder and the coordinate is the city.
stops.campa: He sits for a television programme called Más Arte Más Ciudad and talks about Fernando Botero and a French tribute exhibition. Botero is Medellín's own, the fat volumes that made the city legible to the world after the years when it was legible for other reasons. The recording survives. Its date does not. Nobody logged the broadcast. Whether this is a man of fifty or a man of seventy speaking cannot be said, because there is no birth year to subtract from.

stops.name: Barrio Colombia, the signature as fiador
stops.date_confidence: attested without a date by the December 2025 tribute. No address was found for the cooperative gallery and none of the artists is named; the coordinate is the Barrio Colombia district approximately. The date is a placeholder.
stops.campa: Young artists want to open a cooperative gallery in Barrio Colombia, the old industrial quarter of Medellín whose warehouses turned into studios. No landlord will take them. He signs as their fiador, which in Colombian law means his own assets answer for their rent. A dealer's whole professional life is spent deciding what a thing is worth; here he decides what people are worth and puts his name under the figure. The tribute records it in one sentence and names none of them.
suggested_refs: The cooperative gallery in Barrio Colombia, unnamed and unlocated in every source consulted

stops.name: Bogotá, sculpture enters the Capitolio Nacional
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day: Testigos y Vigías frente a una ciudadanía en flor, Patio Mosquera of the Capitolio Nacional, 19 July to 20 September 2022, the first time sculpture was installed in that space, curated by María del Pilar Rodríguez. The first research round made Restrepo a co-curator; he was not. The tribute casts him and Paola Gutiérrez de Piñeres as apoyo, backing the show. The coordinate is the atlas anchor for Bogotá.
stops.campa: Hugo Zapata's stones stand in the Patio Mosquera of the Capitolio Nacional, the first time sculpture is installed in that courtyard. María del Pilar Rodríguez curates it. Restrepo and Paola Gutiérrez de Piñeres are the backing behind it. Zapata is his close friend, and the friendship gets a national building for a summer, sixty-three days in a courtyard no private dealer ordinarily reaches. The tribute names the friendship and dates nothing else about it, not its start, not a single earlier show.

stops.name: Cartagena de Indias, the museum reopens
stops.date_confidence: the involvement is attested by the December 2025 tribute, which says he helped secure support for a January reopening; the first research round said he funded it and dated it 2022, and both are corrected. The anniversary arithmetic is itself contested, the museum's own history page giving 1979 as its founding while other accounts date the collection to 1972. The coordinate is the Plaza de San Pedro Claver approximately. Not adjudicated.
stops.campa: The Museo de Arte Moderno de Cartagena de Indias, on the plaza beside San Pedro Claver, needs money to open its doors again for what it is calling fifty years. He helps find it. Whether the museum is fifty depends on which founding you accept, 1972 or 1979, and its own history page and its own anniversary do not agree with each other. The doors open in January. He is in Medellín, and the last public act attributed to him is a building six hundred kilometres away that is not his.

stops.name: El Poblado, the impressionist beans
stops.date_confidence: attested without any date by the December 2025 tribute, whose title is built on it. The placeholder puts it in the late years; the practice is described as habitual rather than as a single occasion.
stops.campa: He cooks fríjoles for people. Not caterers and not a cook: he stands at the pot himself and feeds artists, colleagues and friends, and the meal is understood by everyone who receives it as the actual currency of the friendship. When the eulogy comes it will be titled Réquiem a unos fríjoles impresionistas, and the joke inside the title is that a man who sold Picasso and Miró is remembered for a bean stew. The record of the sales is a clause on a website. The record of the beans is an essay.

stops.name: Medellín, the first-class upgrade
stops.date_confidence: attested without a date, a route, an airline, or a named beneficiary. No place at all is given in the source; the coordinate is the city and stands for nothing more. The date is a placeholder.
stops.campa: Artists and colleagues who needed it found their tickets upgraded to first class, paid for by him, unannounced. No route is named, no year, no airline, nobody who received one. It is the sort of thing only friends know and only eulogies print. A dealer spends his life moving objects worth more than the people around him can afford. This is the one recorded instance of him moving a person instead, and the tribute that records it names nobody who sat in the seat.

stops.date_confidence: membership is attested by El Reverbero de Juan Paz; the circle is presided over by Augusto López Valencia. No meeting venue and no date of joining are named in any source, so the coordinate is the city and the date is a placeholder.
stops.campa: Punto Cadeneta is a Medellín tertulia, a standing conversation circle presided over by Augusto López Valencia, and he belongs to it. Where it meets is not written down anywhere; a tertulia needs no address, only a table and the same faces. It is this circle, and not the gallery and not the press, that will announce his death to the city on the morning it happens. The trade knew him as a martillo de subastas. The tertulia knew him as the querido amigo.

stops.date_confidence: attested without any date by the December 2025 tribute, which names the friendship as close. The placeholder puts it in the final year; the friendship itself plainly runs much longer, and no source dates its beginning.
stops.campa: Hugo Zapata cuts landscapes into slate and lets the stone's own bedding decide the image. Restrepo sells him and backs him, and in 2022 puts his work in the Patio Mosquera of the Capitolio Nacional. Every other artist named here arrives attached to a sale or a directory line. This one arrives attached to nothing but the word friend.

stops.name: Medellín, death in the morning
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day by El Reverbero de Juan Paz, whose notice runs the same morning, with a companion Instagram post dated 22 November 2025. stops.campa: He dies in Medellín on a Saturday morning. The notice goes out the same day from his tertulia, one word of time and one of place, and it calls him the querido amigo before it calls him anything professional. No hospital is named, no house, no cause. The coordinate here is the centre of the city and stands for the city. His birth date is still unlocated after every search made; the death is fixed to the morning. One end of the life carries an hour, the other has no year at all.

stops.name: Calle 10, the gallery's notice

The first research round dated it vaguely to December 2025 and flagged as unresolved whether it marked a death, a retirement or an anniversary; falling two days after the death, it is memorial, and the flag is removed.
stops.campa: Two days later the gallery thanks the public for its muestras de cariño and puts its founder in the past tense: almost forty years of his life given to the art world, promoting it, supporting artists. Almost forty from 2025 reaches back to 1986. Its own about page says the gallery began at the start of this century. Its own directory listing says 1991. The staff writing the notice are not counting the room. They are counting the man, and they are the last people to try.

stops.name: Medellín, the arithmetic that does not close
stops.date_confidence: not an event. The date is the day after the tribute and is a placeholder for the state of the record. Every figure named in the campa is quoted from an attested source; no source reconciles them, and this file does not either.
stops.campa: Four counts of one life. Almost forty years, says the gallery in November 2025. Twenty-three years, said El Tiempo in October 2011, which puts the start at 1988. More than thirty years in the sector, says his own about page, undated. More than five decades of cultural vocation, says the tribute, which reaches back past 1975. Set against foundings of 1991 and of the early two thousands, both published by the same gallery. Nothing here adds up, and nothing here is going to be made to.

stops.name: Medellín, the name no encyclopedia carries
stops.date_confidence: state of the record at the time of the search, not an event. Spanish Wikipedia in-site search returned 423 results with none matching, and no English article exists either. The date is a placeholder.
stops.campa: Spanish Wikipedia has no article on him. Neither does English. A man who handled Picasso, Dalí, Miró and Santamaría, who represented the French state mint in Colombia, and who put sculpture into the national Capitol for the first time, leaves no encyclopedia entry, no monograph, and no catalogue under his own name that anyone has found. What he leaves is a paid directory listing, a podcast page, one newspaper article from 2011, and a eulogy about beans.

stops.name: Calle 10, the gallery after him
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction. The gallery was still trading under his name as of the memorial post of 24 November 2025; nothing later was located, so the continuation is inferred and the date is a placeholder. No monument, plaque or street naming was found anywhere.
stops.campa: The rooms on Calle 10 keep his name on the door and the five hundred works on the walls. There is no plaque in Medellín, no street, no monument; the building is the memorial, and it is a working business. A dealer's afterlife is the provenance line: the next time one of those canvases changes hands, a catalogue will print the words ex-collection AH Fine Art, Medellín, and that is the durable form the record of him takes. Nobody reading that line will know about the beans.
